issues.body: The endpoint change widened the read from one directory to the entire registry repository tree. Previously the GitHub contents API guaranteed every entry was inside `orchestration/provenance/`; now that confinement lives entirely in the new line `name = path[len(prefix):] if isinstance(path, str) and path.startswith(prefix) else None`. Every fixture in `_listing` is already inside that directory (two provenance paths, `orchestration/provenance/README.md`, and `{"path": None}`), so the guard is never exercised against a path it must reject. Mutating the line to `name = path.rpartition('/')[2] if isinstance(path, str) else None` — which drops directory scoping entirely — still returns {685} for every assertion in this diff and leaves the self-test fully green. That is a vacuous test of the one line the endpoint switch made load-bearing. The realised failure is a false 'already recorded': any blob anywhere else in the registry repo whose basename matches `<owner>--<name>--pr<N>.json` (a backup/archive copy of the provenance dir, a fixture, an attachment path) would be counted, and census would report a genuinely unrecorded PR as recorded and suppress the mint it should have flagged. No such collision exists in today's layout (`verdict_path` and the round-claim paths carry `-round`/`--r` suffixes that fail `fullmatch`), so this is coverage of a live guard rather than a present-day bug — but the guard is exactly what stops the widened scope from mattering.
issues.fix_hint: Add at least one decoy entry OUTSIDE the provenance directory whose basename would match, and assert it is excluded, e.g. append to `_listing`: `{"path": "orchestration/provenance-archive/" + worker_pr.provenance_path(repo, 686).rpartition("/")[2]}` and `{"path": worker_pr.provenance_path(repo, 687).rpartition("/")[2]}` (a bare basename at repo root). The existing expectation stays {685}; with the prefix guard removed the check goes red on {685, 686, 687}. Consider also asserting a nested path under the directory (`orchestration/provenance/sub/<basename>`) is excluded, and skipping non-blob entries via `entry.get("type") == "blob"`.
issues.title: New directory-scoping guard is untested — the repo-wide tree read has no out-of-directory decoy, so removing `path.startswith(prefix)` keeps --self-test green

issues.body: The retained sentence "a renamed layout reds this rather than silently matching nothing" was true of the contents endpoint: `GET /contents/orchestration/provenance?ref=ledger` 404s when that directory does not exist at the derived path, `_run_gh(check=True)` exits non-zero and `_gh_json` raises MintError. Under `git/trees/{ref}?recursive=1` the request succeeds for any existing ref regardless of whether the directory exists; a renamed/moved `PROVENANCE_DIR` (or a ledger whose records live at the old path) now produces a well-formed, non-truncated tree with zero prefix matches and the function returns `set()`. That collapses "the layout moved out from under me" and "nothing is recorded" into the same answer — the same fail-open shape the rest of the docstring says this function exists to prevent, moved up one level from the file to the directory. Only the read-only census consumes this today, so the consequence is a mis-reported census rather than a duplicate write, but shipping a docstring that asserts a fail-closed property the code no longer has is worse than the behaviour: this repo's docstrings are the audit trail a later reviewer reasons from.
issues.fix_hint: Either restore the signal — after building `numbers`, raise MintError when NO tree entry starts with `directory + "/"` (the ledger's provenance directory always carries at least a README, so this stays quiet in steady state and reds on a rename), and pin it with a self-test passing a tree containing only unrelated paths — or, if the bootstrap case (directory legitimately absent before the first record) must stay non-fatal, delete the now-false sentence and say plainly that a missing directory reads as 'nothing recorded' and only an unreadable/truncated tree raises.
issues.title: Docstring keeps the "a renamed layout reds this" fail-closed claim, but the tree endpoint returns an empty set for a missing/renamed provenance directory

issues.body: `if not isinstance(response, dict) or response.get("truncated") is not False` guards two distinct failures, but only the `truncated: True` case is asserted. The non-dict case is reachable in production: `_gh_json` returns `json.loads(raw or "null")`, so an empty stdout yields `None`, and an error payload such as `{"message": "Not Found"}` takes the missing-`truncated` path — neither is pinned. The previously-deleted assertion covered the `{"message": "Not Found"}` shape explicitly; that coverage was dropped rather than ported.
issues.fix_hint: Add two more cases mirroring the existing pattern: `read_tree=lambda: None` and `read_tree=lambda: {"message": "Not Found"}`, each asserting MintError with "unreadable" in `str(exc)`.
issues.title: The `not isinstance(response, dict)` arm of the first raise has no test

issues.body: The recursive tree lists directories (`type: "tree"`) alongside blobs. A directory named `<owner>--<name>--pr<N>.json` inside the provenance directory would be counted as a recorded record. Unlikely, but the contents-listing version was at least restricted to a single directory's immediate children, and filtering on the type the API already gives you costs one condition.
issues.fix_hint: Match only blobs: `if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("type") == "blob"` before extracting `path`, and add a `{"path": <a matching name>, "type": "tree"}` fixture asserting it is not counted.
issues.title: Tree entries are matched without checking `type == "blob"`

issues.body: It is loop-invariant and the tree is now repo-wide (potentially tens of thousands of entries), so it belongs beside the `numbered` regex rather than inside the loop. Cosmetic only — no behavioural effect.
issues.fix_hint: Hoist `prefix = directory + "/"` to just after the `numbered = re.compile(...)` line.
issues.title: `prefix = directory + "/"` is recomputed on every tree entry

verdict.summary: The motivation is right: `GET /repos/{r}/contents/{dir}` silently caps a directory listing at 1000 entries, so the old `recorded_pr_numbers` read could report a recorded PR as unrecorded once the ledger grew past that — a fail-open on exactly the read backfill's sol #217 flagged. Moving to `git/trees/{ref}?recursive=1` with a strict `truncated is not False` raise fixes that fail-open and fails closed on the new truncation limit, and the added self-test that patches module-global `_gh_json` and pins the exact URL (`repos/reg/istry/git/trees/ledger?recursive=1`) is a genuinely non-vacuous wiring assertion — a revert to the contents endpoint would go red. The truncated-raise and malformed-tree-raise cases are also pinned and non-vacuous. Two things block approval. (1) The read scope silently widened from ONE directory (scoped by the API) to the WHOLE registry repo; the only thing that now confines matches to the provenance directory is the new `path.startswith(prefix)` guard, and no fixture in `_listing` sits outside that directory, so deleting the guard (e.g. `name = path.rpartition('/')[2]`) still yields {685} and the self-test stays green. That is the exact newly-load-bearing line left unkilled. (2) The docstring's fail-closed claim "a renamed layout reds this rather than silently matching nothing" was kept verbatim but is no longer true: with the contents endpoint a missing/renamed provenance directory 404'd and raised; with the tree endpoint it returns a complete tree with zero matches and the function returns an empty set — i.e. "the layout moved" and "nothing is recorded" become the same answer again, for the directory rather than the file. Blast radius is bounded (only the read-only `census` consumes this; the mint write path still probes per-PR via `effective_record_body`), which is why these are major and not blockers, but both are one- or two-line fixes and the docstring is part of this repo's audit trail.
